newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: INTERVIEW-Argentina's Techint to boost investments.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Argentina's Techint to boost investments.

text.p: Argentina's Techint SA, the building and services arm of a group that also controls Siderar and Siderca, plans to invest hundreds of millions of dollars and participate in privatizations in Latin America, CEO Eduardo Baglietto said.
"We plan several investments in what we hope will be the short term," Baglietto, one of four executive vice-presidents at parent Rocca group, told Reuters in an interview Friday.

The group, with annual revenues of $5.5 billion, controls Siderca which, together with Italy's Dalmine and Tubos de Aceros de Mexico, forms a alliance that is a leader in seamless steel tubes for the oil industry. It also controls Siderar, Argentina's leading maker of flat steel.
"In Argentina we are strongly considering taking part in the gas and electricty areas," Baglietto said.

A joint venture of Techint and Chilean companies Central Tocopilla and Edelnor plans to invest more than $400 million to build a gas pipeline from northern Argentina to northern Chile, where there is a strong concentration of mining firms and some steelmakers, Baglietto said.
"We think construction will start no later than October and the pipeline will be operative by the first half of 1999," he said.

At the same time, Techint owns part of Gasinvest, that plans to invest more than $150 million to build another gas pipeline from Entre Rios province to the Brazilian city of Uruguayana where an electric plant is under construction. It will later allow sales to other Brazilian southern areas.
The pipeline will be operated by TGN, which is controlled by Gasinvest, which in turn was set up by Argentina's Comercial del Plata, Canada's Nova Corp and Malaysia's Petronas Dagangang.
"We believe that building will start this year and the gas pipeline be operative towards the end of 1998," he said.
Meanwhile, a consortium headed by Techint is making the final touches on a gas pipeline from La Mora, in Argentina's western Mendoza province, to Santiago.
"We will finish it in June and on August 7 it will inaugurated by Argentina's and Chile's Presidents," Baglietto said. "Next month we have gas flowing to Chile."
In the electrical sector, Techint is considering building two plants of $150 million each for itself, he said.

One, in La Plata, 50 kilometers (30 miles) south of Buenos Aires, would provide steam to Argentine oil group YPF SA and energy to electric firm EDELAP, which is owned by Techint and Houston Lighting and Power Co.
The other one in Bahia Blanca, 500 kilometers (300 miles) south of Buenos Aires, would provide steam and energy to the companies forming a petrochemical complex there.
"We are doing the prefeasibility studies," Baglietto said. "If they are feasible, building of La Plata should start this year and Bahia Blanca this year or early the next."

A 50-50 joint venture set up by Techint and Italy's Snam, controlled by ENI group, is one of the three bidders that prequalified to build a fertilizer plant in Bahia Blanca worth about $500 million for YPF, Argentine industrial holding Perez Companc and Canada's Agrium, Baglietto said.
"We will present our offer in the coming days," he said.
In the telecommunications sector, Techint may bid in 90 days to operate personal communications services (PCS) in Argentina, a new generation of wireless phones.
"This is a project we look upon very favorably. We have the know-how and the experience."

Techint was a founding member of Cointel, the holding that controls Telefonica de Argentina. Last month Techint sold to Telefonica de Espana its remaining 8.3 percent stake in Cointel for $240 million.
Baglietto said Techint also plans to actively participate in privatization drives in other Latin American countries where it already has a presence.

"We will participate in the privatization of the gas distribution in Bogota. We will try our hand at the privatization of Ecuador's phone company, Emetel, and in the gas Brazilian gas sector privatization once that country frees its regulations."
He added that Siderar, the seamless tube maker of Rocca group, was seriously studying bidding for Venezuela's steelmaker Siderurgica del Orinoco (Sidor).
((--Buenos Aires Newsroom, 541 318-0650))
